# Bare email addresses

alex@example.com

Write to alex@example.com about it.

Write to alex@example.com.

Write to alex@example.com, then wait.

Write to first.last-name_x+tag@mail.example.co.uk today.

- In a list item, alex@example.com.

> In a blockquote, alex@example.com.

Not in a code span: `alex@example.com`.

Not in an autolink: <alex@example.com>.

Not as a destination: [write](mailto:alex@example.com).

In link text: [alex@example.com](mailto:alex@example.com).

No dot in the domain: alex@localhost here.

Domain ends in a dash: alex@example.com- here.

Domain ends in an underscore: alex@example.com_ here.

Domain ends in a digit: alex@example.123 here.

Label ends in a dash: alex@exa-.com here.

Letter before the local part is part of it: xalex@example.com here.

After a slash: path/alex@example.com here.

After a colon: to:alex@example.com here.

After an opening parenthesis: (alex@example.com) here.

After an asterisk: *alex@example.com* here.

With mailto: mailto:alex@example.com here.

Inside a URL: https://example.com/alex@example.com here.

Two on a line: alex@example.com and bob@example.com.

Emphasis inside: **alex@example.com** here.

Underscores around: _alex@example.com_ here.

Trailing dots: alex@example.com... here.

Empty local part: @example.com here.

Twice at: alex@@example.com here.

Hyphen in the domain: alex@my-example.com here.

Domain ends after a dot and a letter: alex@example.com.x here.

Underscore in the domain: alex@ex_ample.c_m here.

Underscore starts the local part: _alex@example.com here.

Dot starts the local part: .alex@example.com here.

Escaped underscore before: \_alex@example.com here.

In brackets: [alex@example.com] here.

After brackets: [x] alex@example.com here.

After an unclosed bracket: [x alex@example.com here.

A URL in link text: [https://example.com](https://example.com).

A URL after an unclosed bracket: [x https://example.com here.

A directive before: ab:alex@example.com here.

A directive name ending in a dash: :alex-@example.com here.

A directive before a URL: see:https://example.com here.

Two colons: a::alex@example.com here.

A digit after the colon: a:1alex@example.com here.
